title: Chopin’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.text:
[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage. For composers outside the symphonic tradition it asks for an honest counterfactual.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Chopin’s Missing Symphony (work id chopin-symphony-1)

Honest counterfactual: Chopin wrote no symphony, and nothing for orchestra without a solo piano. Everything he composed starts from the keyboard. This work asks what four of his genres might become if an orchestra had to play them without a piano: a sonata first movement, a nocturne, a mazurka and a krakowiak. It is new music; no theme is taken from Chopin, and it is not an orchestration of any piano piece.

How the piano writing is translated: the singing right hand goes to clarinet, flute or violins; its ornaments are written out as triplets and sixteenth notes; the left hand’s wide broken chords go to a harp, which I have added to the orchestra of his concertos for that purpose, over held strings; the mazurka’s drone fifths go to cellos, basses and horns.

Orchestra (13 staves, sounding pitch): pairs of flutes, oboes, clarinets and bassoons, four horns, two trumpets, timpani in B and F sharp, harp, strings.

Movements
I. Allegro maestoso, B minor, 4/4: a grave dotted theme; a nocturne-like second theme in D for clarinet over harp, repeated with decoration; as in his second and third piano sonatas the reprise leaves out the first theme and begins with the transition; it ends in B major, where the first theme finally returns in the coda.
II. Nocturne: Larghetto, G major, 12/8: a long melody over harp arpeggios, repeated with ornament by the flute; an agitated recitative in G minor in the middle.
III. Tempo di mazurka, B minor, with a Trio in B major over a drone, with the raised fourth of Polish folk music.
IV. Rondo à la krakowiak: Vivace, B major, 2/4, with the dance’s syncopated rhythm.

Target length about thirteen minutes. Compromise known from the start: melodies, ornaments and the chord of every bar are written by hand; a program writes the harp figuration, held chords, tutti textures and brass from the chord plan.

First playable draft: the whole first movement — a grave B minor theme, a nocturne-like second theme for clarinet over harp, and a reprise that, as in Chopin's sonatas, skips the first theme and ends in B major.

First complete draft: added the Nocturne in G over harp arpeggios, the Mazurka with its drone Trio, and the Rondo à la krakowiak. A revision pass follows.

Revision pass: the Nocturne's last return has a new, more elaborate ornamented line; the harp, which was silent after the second movement, now plays in the Mazurka's Trio and in the introduction and D major episode of the finale.
